title: Robust Event Forecasting with Spatiotemporal Confounder Learning

problem.claim: Data-driven societal event forecasting must predict future events from historical information despite limited or poor-quality labeled data.

gap.claim: Causal effect estimation for event forecasting is difficult because events occur in complex dynamic environments with hidden confounders and spatiotemporal non-IID data.

contributions.claim: A deep learning framework integrates causal effect estimation into event forecasting.
A causal inference model estimates individual treatment effects from observational event data with spatiotemporal attributes.
Robust learning modules inject learned causal information into event prediction through feature reweighting and an approximate constraint loss.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe their causal inference model for spatiotemporal observational event data as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report evaluating the causal inference model on real-world event datasets.
The authors report validating the robust learning modules by feeding learned causal information into different deep learning methods for event prediction.
The authors report strengths of the causal inference model for individual treatment effect estimation and beneficial properties of the robust learning modules for societal event forecasting.

narrative_sequence.summary: Data-driven methods use historical information to forecast societal events but depend on labeled data quality and availability.
Causal analysis may improve robustness, but hidden confounders and spatiotemporal non-IID structure make causal estimation difficult.
The work introduces a deep learning framework with a novel individual treatment effect model and causal-information injection modules.
The authors evaluate the model and robust learning modules on real-world event datasets and across different deep learning methods.
The authors report strengths in treatment effect estimation and benefits for societal event forecasting.

source_observation.claim: Hidden confounders affect both potential causes and outcomes in societal event data.

interpretation.claim: Forecasting methods may be more robust when they model confounding structure instead of relying only on correlations.

application.claim: Use causal effect estimation and learned causal information as prior knowledge for event forecasting.

exception.claim: Causal estimation may remain difficult when the social environment is dynamic and the data are spatiotemporally non-IID.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the real-world datasets, forecasting targets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the causal assumptions, model architecture, or implementation details.
